FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard (First Rcvrsionj was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalised by trie Cosmeiics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related 
Products Division Council 

Shaving lotions are offered as either prc-shavc or nflcr-shavc P re-shave preparations arc generally of two 
types, a) those intended primarily to -.often the beard and having a ■wetting agent as the active ingredient 
in a base of alcohol, water and glycerine, perl timed and tinted, and b) those ql ling like strong astringents 
which contract the skin, making ihe hair stand straight 

This standard was first issued m 197'J In this revision, two types of afier-shavc lonons, namely, alcoholic 
and non-alcoholic have been incorporated In addition method of determination of alcohol content has 
been revised and a list ol suitahle dcnaiuranis which are commonly used for alcoholic cosmetic prepara- 
tion has been included lor manufacturers' reference Also Ihe requirements for stability of perfume and 
transparency above 5"C luce been spccilicd 

After-shave lotions are usually similar in composition to astringent lotions, with varying percentage of 
alcohol (0 to 7(J percent) which serves to cool the skin The alcohol when present also serves as mild 
annseplic lo aid against inlcciion Addition, il materials like humetlant and menthol (lor cooling and 
anaesthetic aetionj are Irequenlh added l! is alsoiallcd aflei-shave moislunscr. 

After-shave lotions arc usually transparent soluli' ms and are sometimes made translucent or opaque with 
clouding or opaeihing agents Thus, allci -shave lot hi ns aie available both as clear transparent solutions 
and opaque solutions 

Il is necessary thai the raw materials used an. such that in the concentrations in which they would be 
present m the finished after-shave lotion, allei mtciaction with the other raw materials used in the 
formulation are Iree Ironi am haimhil c Heels [ m determining the suitability of a new furmulalion or 
new raw material used in an old formulation, lelciince may be made to IS 41)11 : 19S2. It shall be the 
responsibility of (lie manulacluicr ol alicr-sltave lotion to satisfy llself ot the dermalological and 
microbiological safely ol their iornmlalion according to IS 4U1! . 1°S2 and Indian standard on 
microbiological safely of cosmetics (under piepaianon) respectively before releasing the product for sale. 

For Ihe purpose ol deciding u he Ihci a pailicular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 ■ I960 'Rules for rounding oil numeiaal values (itMsed)' The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as thai ol the specified value in this standard.

IS 9255 : 1995 



Indian Standard 
AFTERSHAVE LOTION — SPECIFICATION 



( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirement arid 
methods of sampling and test for after-shave lot ion. 

2 NORMATIVE REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary ad- 
juncts to this standard. The standards contain 
provisions which through reference in this text 
constitute provisions of this standard. At the time 
of publication, the editions indicated were valid. 
All standards arc subject to revision, and parties 
to agreements based on this standard are en- 
couraged to investigate the possibility of applying 
the most recent revisions of theslandardsindicatcd 
below

3 TYPE 

There shall "be two types of alicr-shavc lotions, 
namely: 

l) Type 1 — Alcoholic, containing 5 to 7U per- 
cent alcohol, and 

n) Type 2 — Non-alcoholic. 



4 REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 Description 

4.1.1 Alcoholic — It shall be a transparent/trans- 
luccnt/opaque aqueous ethanolic or emulsified 
solution containing perfume oil and shall be free 
from sediment. It may also contain emollients, an- 
tiseptic agents, denaturants, astringents, colouring 
agents, etc. 

4.1.2 Non-Alcohohc — It shall be a transparent/ 
translucent/opaque aqueous or emulsified solution 
containing perfume oil and shall be free from sedi- 
ment. It may also contain emollients, antiseptic 
agents, astringents, colouring agents etc 

4.2 Ingredients 

fJnfess specified 1 otherwise, all the raw materials 
used in the manufacture of after-shave lotion shall 
conform to the requirements prescribed in the 
relevant Indian Standards where such standards 
exist. Alcohol used in the Type 1 after-shave lotion 
shall conform to IS 323 : 1959 and it shall be free 
from methanol when tested in accordance with 16 
of IS 3752:1988. 

4.3 The dyes/colours used in the manufacture of 
after-shave lotion shall comply with the provisions 
of IS 4707 (Part 1) : 1988. Ingredients other than 
dyes/colours shall comply with the provisions of 
IS 4707 (Part 2): 1993. 

4.4 Composition 

4.4.1 Typel after-shave lotion shall contain 5 to 70 
percent (vjv) alcohol, when tested by the method 
prescribed in Annex A. 

4.4.2 List of suitable denaturants which arccon- 
sidered lexicologically safe for use in alcoholic cos- 
metic preparations is given in Annex B. 

4.5 Stability of Smell 

4.5.1 When tested in accordance with the test 
method as specified in 4.5.2, after 8 hours Ihesmell 
of alter-shave lotion shall be clearly picked up. 

4.5.2 Put some pieces of bleached gauze of dimen- 
sions 5 x 10 cm, which has been pre-washed in hot 
water without soap and dried, into a porcelain cup 



1 



IS 925S 1 1995 



and pour l.S ml of after-shave lotion into this cup. 
After the gauze gets soaked lake it out with the help 
of pincers and without squeezing it, dry it in a 
premise having temperature 27±2°C and humidity 
65±5%. If after 8 hours, Ihe smell of after-shave 
lotion can be clearly picked up, the product shall be 
taken to have passed the test. 

4.6 Claud Temperature 

4.6.1 When tested in accordance with the test 
method as specified in 4.6.2, at a temperature of 5°C 
the after-shave lotion shall be transparent. 

4.6.2 This requirement is applicable for clear 
transparent after-shave lotions only Pour 20 ml 
after-shave lotion into a wide cylinder and close it 
with a plug, into which insert a thermometer having 
scale uplo-20°C. Immerse the thermometer into 
the liquid in such a manner thai jis bulb is situated 
at the same distance from the bottom and walls 
Immerse the cylinder containing liquid in a cooling 
mixture containing ice and salt. After cooling the 
sample to + 5°C, takeout the cylinder, shake it and 
scan it in transmuted daylight or in the light of a 40 
W electric lamp. At a temperature of +5 C the 
product shall be taken to have passed l he test if no 
turbidity appears. 

5 PACKING AND MAUK1NG 

5.1 The aftershave Lotion shall be packed in 
suitable well-closed containers. 

5.2 The containers shall be legibly marked with the 
following information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Manufacturer's name and its recognized 
trade mark, if any; 



c) Net volume of the material; 

d) List of critical ingredients; 

e) Batch number; 

f) Name and content of denaturant, if added ; 
and 

g) A caution sign given below : (for Type 1 
only) 

'HARMFUL IF TAKEN INTERNALLY'; 

or 
the words 'ALCOHOL FREE" (for Type 2 
products only). 

5.3 BIS Certification Marking 

5.3.1 Each package may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

5.3.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there- 
under. The details of conditions under which the 
licence for Ihe use of Standard Mark may be granted 
m manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6 SAMPLING 

6.1 Representative samples of the material shall be 
drawn as prescribed in IS 3958 : 19S4. 

6.2 Test for all characteristics shall be carried out 
on ihe composite sample. 

6.3 The material shall be taken to have conformed 
to this standard if the composite sample passes all 
the tests. 



ANNEX A 

(Clause 4.4.1) 
METHOD OF TEST FOR ALCOHOL CONTENT IN AFTER-SIIAVE LOTION 



A-l DETERMINATION OF ALCOHOL 

CONTENT 

A-l.l Reagents 

a) Sodium chloride, 

b) Hcxane, 

c) Sodium hydroxide-l N, and 

d) Phenolphthalein (solid), 

A-l. 2 Procedure 

Take 25 ml of the sample, accurately measured at 
25 C C, in a separator. Add 101) ml of water and mix, 
saturate this mixture with sodium chloride, then 
add 100 ml of hexane and shake the mixture 



vigorously for two to three minutes. Allow the mix- 
ture to stand for about 15 to 20 minutes. Run the 
lower layer intu the distillation ilask, wash the 
hcxane in the separator by washing vigorously with 
about 25 ml of sodium chloride solution to stand 
and run the wash liquor into the first saline solu- 
tion. Make the mixed solution just alkaline with 
sodium hydroxide with solid phenolphthalein as 
indicator. Add a little pumice powder and 100 ml 
of water Distill and collect not less than 90 ml of 
d ist] 11a te into an 100 ml volumetric flask. Adj ust the 
temperature at 25°C and dilute with water to 100 
ml at ihe same temperature. Determine the specific 
gravity at 25°C Find the percentage (V/vJof ethyl 
alcohol corresponding to the specific gravity by 



IS 9255 1 1995 

reference lo the cthly alcohol tables (see IS 3506 : distillate. Multiply by 4 to gel Ihe percentage of 
1989). This iigure gives the alcohol content of the ethyl alcohol in the sample.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued lo standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also
